instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. For the prediction below, answer two questions. (a) COULD IT FAIL: is there a result, stated or plainly implied in the wording, that would count against it, and that a study could actually observe? (b) DOES IT SEPARATE the theory from a rival: does at least one theory on the list of rivals predict something different (not merely stay silent)? If yes, name the rival or rivals, and say whether your view of the rival comes from the material given or from your own knowledge. Answer in JSON: {"could_fail": true|false, "separates": true|false, "separates_from": [ids], "rival_view_from": "material"|"own knowledge"|"both"|"none", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "..."}.

core_claim.quote: My bet is that boundary, mattering, self-awareness and kept memory make experience richer, and that none of them is known to switch it on.

source.citation: Fredrickson JA. Working Positions. Sentient Horizons, latest revision shown on the page 2026-10-24

prediction.statement: Removing a boundary, mattering, self-awareness or kept memory makes experience poorer but does not switch it off.

first_stated.passage: If removing one of the four features I call enriching turned out to switch experience off, that feature would move from enriching to required.

source.citation: Fredrickson JA. Working Positions. Sentient Horizons, latest revision shown on the page 2026-10-24

prediction.test_for: Cases where one of the four is removed (for example, kept memory, as in Henry Molaison's case, which the page cites) and experience goes on.
prediction.test_against: Removing one of the four switches experience off.

what_the_sources_say_about_rivals.statement: Damasio's theory puts 'affect and feeling at the core' of consciousness (Seth and Bayne's Table 1, as quoted in the theory-list report), so it predicts that removing mattering switches experience off.
